scope: A shared pure C map kernel and typed SDK bridge upload currently locked bound VBs before normal draws and VBs plus IB before indexed draws. All metadata is validated before the first upload, repeated bindings upload once, genuine readonly maps upload nothing, and nonindexed draws leave the mapped IB pending. Every draw observes the current mapped bytes while Lock offsets/sizes/state remain intact; only an accepted unique upload consumes DISCARD. Accepted prefix receipts are committed even if a later buffer fails; no Draw or ClipStatus/mirror commit follows that failure. Upload callbacks may themselves have accepted transport chunks before reporting failure; retrying their complete mapped range safely starts a new discard when required. Software Draw input explicitly permits mapped sources, while public ProcessVertices input stays strict. Zero-primitive draws do not flush maps. Actual production Draw functions validate upload-before-Draw ordering, duplicate bindings, held software source classification and failure/status atomicity. Actual SDK Lock/Unlock plus distinct VB/IB native layouts cover seventeen maps, exact data/ranges, repeated writes, readonly/static/conflicting hints, zero-size maps, prefixes and retained locks. Real XP produces 42 frames over two owners with 98 exact updates; tests preserve first-triangle bytes across partial writes, skip genuine readonly uploads, retain NOOVERWRITE flags without rewriting in-flight data, exercise 32-bit indices and defer IB discard/upload across nonindexed draws. SwiftShader/Metal each pass 126 color probes. Existing three-API TNL/state-block/lifetime and D3D9 typed/color/multi-stream/ProcessVertices lock boundaries pass in XP. Published D3D8/9 DLLs are the exact accepted mapped probe bytes. This addresses the four originally listed S2-34 hint/base/zero/locked-draw cases across 4H2a/b without claiming original Microsoft mapped-buffer pixel observations or a complete Draw/UP/missing-binding API audit. Remaining retail copy semantics, guest wrappers, programmable CPU processing and stages 4/5/6 continue.
